query: Resorts World committed annually, for the license term, the lesser of 2 percent of incremental GGR above 2025 levels or $25 million to a workforce housing fund.

facts.text: For the license term RWNYC promised the workforce housing fund the annual lesser of $25 million or 2% of incremental GGR above 2025 levels.
The Board proposed alternative ways of addressing benefits originally projected beyond the awarded license term.
RWNYC's original license term is 15 years.
The Cirrus partnership agreement defines annual commitments as calendar-year cash capital contributions.
RWNYC's housing dashboard reported $25 million delivered in 2026 through September.
Official records show a $46.125 million deed for the Jamaica acquisition dated May 29, 2026.
Official records show a $24 million mortgage accompanying the Jamaica acquisition.
The recorded buyer of the Jamaica parcel was RWNYC ARCHER AVE LLC.
The recorded parcel was Queens block 10151, lot 39, at 92-02 165 Street.
Trade reporting links Cirrus WFHA Funding and Resorts World to the Jamaica acquisition.
RWNYC described 700 Jamaica workforce housing units as proposed.
The August 2026 PLUTO record listed zero residential units on the Jamaica parcel.

conditions.text: RWNYC actually transferred the qualifying housing-fund contribution for the license year under review.
The transferred amount matched the annual lesser-of formula using the relevant increment above 2025 GGR.

reference_verdict.reasoning: Retain partially corroborated, Medium confidence and pending human review. City indexes independently establish acquisition and financing metadata, including the legal buyer; they do not trace RWNYC cash into the property. RWNYC explicitly claims $25M delivered in 2026 through September, but no dated recipient receipt, capital ledger or GGR reconciliation verifies annual compliance. Keep the Cirrus platform, partnership and title SPV separate. The 700 homes remain proposed. Term treatment, contribution timing, affordability conditions and the cash chain require further records; missing evidence does not establish nonpayment.

sources.title: GFLB Selection Document December 2025
sources.citation: GFLB, 1 December 2025, PDF p.25 / printed p.24; PDF p.10 / printed p.9, footnote 5
sources.publisher: New York State Gaming Facility Location Board
sources.locator: GFLB, 1 December 2025, PDF p.25 / printed p.24; PDF p.10 / printed p.9, footnote 5
sources.specific_evidence: The regulator records the annual lesser-of formula. Footnote 5 offers proportional reduction or funding within awarded years for commitments beyond the awarded term; the reviewed record does not establish which option the Commission adopted.
sources.notes: Independent regulatory record of an applicant pledge, not payment evidence. No verified installment schedule, zero floor, or fixed $375M/$750M total follows from this passage.

sources.title: RWNYC Gaming Facility License
sources.citation: NYS Gaming Commission, 19 December 2025, PDF pp.1, 3-5; Conditions 3, 5 and 10
sources.locator: NYS Gaming Commission, 19 December 2025, PDF pp.1, 3-5; Conditions 3, 5 and 10
sources.specific_evidence: The actual license establishes an initial 15-year term and requires community benefit budgets, progress reporting and independent monitoring. These requirements identify records that could test A034 performance but do not themselves establish a housing payment or resolve longer package projections.
sources.notes: Independent governing instrument. The selected public meeting materials reviewed supplied no housing payment reconciliation; this is a bounded search finding, not evidence of nonpayment.

sources.title: Exhibit 175 Resorts World Cirrus WFH Partnership Agreement
sources.citation: 2025-05-15 execution version; posted 2026-05-05; PDF pp.4, 10-11, 17; Article III pp.19-26
sources.publisher: RWNYC application, hosted by New York State
sources.locator: 2025-05-15 execution version; posted 2026-05-05; PDF pp.4, 10-11, 17; Article III pp.19-26
sources.specific_evidence: The agreement identifies Genting New York LLC, Resorts World Cirrus WFH, LP and general partner Cirrus WFH RW GP, LLC. Annual commitments are defined as calendar-year cash capital contributions, but operative capital details were unavailable in the retrieved public text.
sources.notes: Party-authored document; hosting does not verify funding. PDF images and signatures were not authenticated. No receiving account, capital call or 2026 cash receipt was established.

sources.title: RWNYC Community Investments Dashboard
sources.citation: Workforce Housing Fund card, web lines 159-170; data as of September 2026; reviewed by 4 November 2026
sources.locator: Workforce Housing Fund card, web lines 159-170; data as of September 2026; reviewed by 4 November 2026
sources.specific_evidence: RWNYC reports $25 million delivered in 2026 under its Workforce Housing Fund program, with data through September. The card provides an explicit annual program claim but no payee, transfer date, capital account acknowledgment or reconciliation to the GGR formula.
sources.notes: Company self-report, not independent cash verification. Keep separate from the acquisition price and historical down payment; do not code full annual compliance as verified.

sources.title: Cirrus WFHA Funding and Resorts World NYC Jamaica Acquisition Report
sources.citation: New York Real Estate Journal, 28 July 2026, opening acquisition paragraphs and participant quotations
sources.locator: New York Real Estate Journal, 28 July 2026, opening acquisition paragraphs and participant quotations

sources.notes: External publication relaying transaction participants, not an independent fund audit. Acquisition association does not establish SPV ownership, annual contribution amount or the receiving legal entity.

sources.locator: Impact card and Jamaica acquisition paragraph; data as of September 2026; reviewed by 4 November 2026

sources.publisher: NYC Department of City Planning via NYC Open Data

sources.specific_evidence: The August 2026 PLUTO parcel record names RWNYC Archer as owner and lists zero residential units and zero residential area. It corroborates the existing nonresidential asset at that snapshot, without establishing conditions on the November research cutoff date.
sources.notes: Independent administrative data, not a site inspection. Do not infer universal absence of approvals or later work, or treat 700 proposed units as delivered homes.

workbook_fields.page_section: pdf p.25; Resorts World: Local Impact Siting
workbook_fields.commitment_text: Resorts World has offered a community benefits package consisting of an annual commitment, for the duration of the license term, of the lesser of 2 percent of incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels, or $25 million per year for a workforce housing fund.
workbook_fields.normalized_statement: Resorts World committed annually, for the license term, the lesser of 2 percent of incremental GGR above 2025 levels or $25 million to a workforce housing fund.
workbook_fields.responsible_entity: Genting New York LLC d/b/a Resorts World New York City
workbook_fields.amount_value: lesser of 2 percent of incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels, or $25 million per year
workbook_fields.term_periodicity: annual; for the duration of the license term
workbook_fields.condition_contingency: amount depends on incremental gross gaming revenue above 2025 levels (zero if none)
workbook_fields.milestone: investments to begin "in the immediate term" (undated)
workbook_fields.adjudication_note: Firm 'annual commitment' but amount is revenue-contingent; competing label Contractual commitment. Commitment assumed a 30-year term vs 15-year license (see conflict row).
workbook_fields.notes: Formula transcribed, not computed. Board urges Commission and CAC officials to monitor implementation. | Web evidence 2026-10-14 (no public evidence located -> partially corroborated): First project under the RW-Cirrus initiative: 92-30 165th St, Jamaica (~700 units) acquired for $46.125M by Cirrus WFHA Funding 'in partnership with Resorts World' [S12, S13]. No source ties the purchase to the annual 2%/$25M fund, and RW's supplement frames it as '$750 million ... up to $25 million per year' [S05].
